title: IBM Stretch and the First Pipelined Computer (1961)
explainer: The IBM 7030 "Stretch," delivered in 1961, pioneered instruction pipelining, operand prefetch, and even speculative execution with branch-misprediction recovery — techniques usually associated with 1990s superscalar CPUs — decades before they became mainstream. It was considered a commercial failure at the time (it fell well short of its 100x-speedup goal), but nearly every aggressive pipelining idea in this lesson has a lineage traceable back to Stretch's design team, several of whom later architected the IBM System/360.

title: Tomasulo's Algorithm and the IBM System/360 Model 91 (1967)
explainer: Robert Tomasulo's 1967 paper, "An Efficient Algorithm for Exploiting Multiple Arithmetic Units," introduced register renaming, reservation stations, and a common data bus to let the IBM System/360 Model 91 execute floating-point instructions out of order while still producing correct, in-order-looking results. The algorithm sat largely unused for over twenty years before reappearing, essentially unchanged in spirit, as the backbone of 1990s superscalar out-of-order processors — and it still carries its inventor's name today.
